newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan buying wheat, stays out on corn/soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan buying wheat, stays out on corn/soybeans.

text.p: Taiwanese buyers are expected to retender for 68,000 tonnes of wheat this week, but remain out of the corn and soybean markets with shipments of these products being pushed further back, traders said on Monday.
The retender for two 34,000-tonne shipments of U.S. wheat for May and June delivery is due to be held on Wednesday.

The outbreak of foot and mouth disease, which has devastated the country's pork industry and hit imports of feed corn, has had relatively little impact on wheat, which forms only a small part of animal feed consumption.

The Kaohsiung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association was considering tendering for 54,000 tonnes of soybeans for June delivery, but backed down because of the excess soymeal inventories being held by buyers.
Traders said they did not expect any fresh corn tenders either as buyers also try to reduce stocks in this sector.

Taiwan on Thursday returned to the world corn market for the first time since the government reported the outbreak of the hog foot and mouth epidemic on March 20 and ordered a pork export ban and islandwide drive to slaughter or inoculate 14 million pigs.

The FGEP buying group bought a 54,000-tonne U.S. corn shipment pegged for July delivery. Traders said the purchase showed Taiwan's corn buyers were still working on trimming their supplies as the shipment was so far in the future.
"Normally the FGEP group's April tender would set shipment for late May to June delivery, but Thursday's shipment is for July," a corn trader said.
Grain traders have said Taiwan's 1997 corn imports would fall significantly from 1996 due to the disease outbreak, which has sharply reduced demand for feed.
Taiwan importers have cancelled several corn tenders and at least one purchased shipment in the wake of the announcement of the mass slaughter of the island's hogs.

In a Reuters Poll conducted on April 15, corn buyers and traders from six key grain firms all forecast imports that would fall sharply from 1996, when Taiwan bought about 6.5 million tonnes of corn, according to private estimates.
The poll forecast Taiwan's 1997 corn imports would range from just 4.9 million tonnes to as high as 5.8 million tonnes and averaged about 5.19 million tonnes.

U.S. Pacific Northwest to Taiwan freight rates were estimated at about US$14.00 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico at around $24.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipment.
